decisions.reason: This safety shoe line sits at the heart of the firm's existing footwear knowledge and production capabilities, so a large established producer with in-house development is likely to retain and refine it rather than withdraw it.

A comfort insole is closely related to the firm's core shoe business and can be learned from through existing product-development and fit expertise, although its lower website prominence makes it slightly more droppable than the main footwear lines.
A supportive insole also builds on the firm's established knowledge of work-shoe fit and user needs, so absorptive capacity is high and the product is more likely to be improved than discontinued.

An ergonomic safety shoe series is strongly aligned with the firm's core competence in protective footwear and was prominent enough to have its own page, indicating commitment and a low likelihood of withdrawal.
Firefighter and rescue boots are a more specialised extension of protective footwear, but they still draw heavily on the firm's related safety-boot knowledge, making retention more likely than exit.

This moulded insole was presented as a flagship direction and shown on the home page, which together with the firm's strong related knowledge suggests very low odds of being taken off the market soon.
